_help: The traveling merchant (Scripts/traveling_merchant_spawner.gd + traveling_merchant.gd). Edit and restart to tune.
He is not always around: after the server starts he first shows up after a random number of minutes in 'first_visit_delay_minutes',
and after each visit he is gone for a random number of minutes in 'visit_gap_minutes' (both [min, max], real-world minutes).
A visit: he appears at the 'spawn' marker, walks to the 'dock' marker and trades there for 'dock_stay_seconds', walks to the town
'gate' marker and trades there for 'gate_stay_seconds', then packs up and disappears. He only trades while he is standing still.
Markers are node paths in the zone scene (the Markers node). *_stand_offset moves where he stands, relative to the marker [x, y, z],
so he does not stand on top of another NPC. walk_speed is metres per second. shop_id is a key in Data/vendor_shop.json: THAT is his stock.
model is a key of Player3D.CHARACTER_MODELS (a race + sex, e.g. halfling_male, human_male, half_orc_female). Lines are picked at random.
greeting = hail or right-click at a stop; ambient = said to nearby players every 1-2 minutes while he trades (at night a 20% chance it is a 'secret' line instead);
sales = said when his shop opens; token_surprise = his reaction (once per visit per player) if you are carrying a Ceramic Water-Token. quest_hooks is kept here for the quest system to use.

Lines: greeting / ambient / sales / secret / quest_hooks are the user's own text (with {keyword} markup added). Everything in 'topics' plus busy, warn, farewell, hail_leaving, token_surprise_emote, wrong_item are DRAFTS in his voice, awaiting approval.

topics: see Scripts/npc_conversation.gd. {word} in a line is a clickable keyword; what the player says near him (typed /say or clicked) picks the first topic whose keyword matches and whose 'requires' hold.
name: Sahren of the Deep Wells

greeting: Traveler! You look like someone seeking what others cannot find. I am Sahren, of the {Djhanid}.
Ah, a new face. Care to {browse} the wonders of distant sands?
Welcome. My {goods} come from places the Bastion guards only whisper about.
You carry the scent of the road. A fellow wanderer, perhaps? Mind the {dangers} of these sands.
ambient: Maps lie. The desert does not.
Careful with that relic - it remembers its last owner.
{Djhanid} craftwork... priceless to some, dangerous to others.
Storm winds carried strange whispers last night.
sales: Everything here has a story. Some even have teeth.
Looking for charms? Relics? Spices? Secrets?
Prices shift like dunes - but for you, I can be reasonable.
If you see something glowing, don't touch it. Ask me first.
A fair trade is a happy trade.
secret: My people walk where shadows have weight.
The tomb guardians do not sleep. They wait.
Ghost caravans cross the dunes still. I've seen them.
Djhanid blood remembers things the mind forgets.
quest_hooks: A relic fragment lies somewhere between Sandcrest Landing and Thallia's Bastion. Bring it to me.
A caravan vanished on the northern route. If you find any trace, I must know.
There's a Djhanid charm buried beneath the sands - humming with power. I need someone brave.
A Bastion courier stole something from me. Recover it, and I'll owe you a favor.
token_surprise: Where did you get {that}? Do you know what this is {for}?
token_surprise_emote: {name} goes very still, his eyes on the clay disc in your pack.
busy: The sands do not wait, friend. Find me when I have stopped.
Walk beside me if you like, but I trade only at rest.
warn: The shadows lengthen. Soon I walk on.
Choose your treasures, friend. My feet grow restless.
farewell: The sands call, and I answer. Until our paths cross again.
May your water never run low.
hail_leaving: Quickly, quickly. The road is waiting.
wrong_item: Sahren looks at it, then at you. "That is not what I am looking for."

lines: You have taken up the task. Bring me three {tokens}: drag them from your pack onto me.
The sands are quieter, thanks to you. I have no more of this task for you, for now.

sequence: You would do this? Then listen closely. The {Hollowed} wander the deep dunes, where the sun hangs directly over their shadows.
When they are at rest, take what they carry: a clay {token}, like the one I showed you. Bring me three.
Drag them from your pack onto me, and I will know the sands are quieter.

lines: They still wander. Every one you release is a soul the sun no longer holds.
Some still wander, I am sure. But you have done what my people could not.

sequence: The Hollowed. That is what we call those who broke the code and were sent out into the wastes.
We believe a soul is carried in the shadow. At noon, when the sun stands over you and your shadow vanishes, that is when the madness comes in.
My people will not raise a hand against them. The taint would follow us home. But someone must {release} them.
Softly. That mark... it belonged to one of my people who broke the code.
Whoever carried it had walked among the {Hollowed}.

lines: A clay disc stamped with our mark. A debt of {water}, made solid. If you ever find one far from the deep wells, bring it to me. Do not spend it. Do not sell it.

sequence: In the sands, coin is heavy and useless. Water is the only true coin.
So we keep our debts in clay. Each {token} is a measure of water, stored in a deep well that only my people can find.
To you it is pottery. To a Djhanid, it is a life.
We are the Djhanid: wanderers of the dunes, where the wind itself keeps house.
Outsiders find our camps and see nothing. We do not build. We anchor our shelters to the wind, and the sand does the rest.
We trust little that is not the desert. We keep our {water}, and we keep our code.
Sand stingers lie buried in the dunes, waiting for a careless step. Their venom is why we tip our blades.
The sand itself can rise and walk. Strike a sandshifter when it is still, not when it moves.
And beware the Dustwalkers. They wear cloth like ours, but they are not my people. You will know them by what they do.

lines: Why do I trade? A Djhanid could keep to the dunes, and most do. I prefer the road: every stranger is a story, and the sands look different at every step.
Everything here has a story. Some even have teeth. Look, and choose.
Prices shift like dunes - but for you, I can be reasonable.
